source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Classify a planet and place the eight planets in their correct order and broad inner-outer groups.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Inner: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune; outer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: All eight planets are mostly made of gases.

intelligence.enrichment: A planet is a large, nearly spherical object that revolves around the Sun; the eight planets in increasing distance from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, with the first four as inner planets and the last four as large gaseous outer planets. Revolution around the Sun and nearly spherical shape identify a planet, while distance from the Sun determines the ordered sequence and the inner or outer grouping. The learner correctly applies this rule: A planet is a large, nearly spherical object that revolves around the Sun; the eight planets in increasing distance from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, with the first four as inner planets and the last four as large gaseous outer planets. A planet is any round object seen in space, and the eight planets can be ordered by size or brightness.
